mainTopic: The תיובתא against רבא about the רקיע, ברייתות about astronomy, and רבי אליעזר's threshold rule for דרך רחוקה in קרבן פסח
overview: This amud opens at the end of a ברייתא that the גמרא quoted against רבא. In it, a בת קול answers נבוכדנצר's boast: a person lives only 70 or 80 years, while the heavens are thousands of years' walk away. The ברייתא says the רקיע is 500 years thick, which contradicts רבא, so the גמרא declares a תיובתא. Next comes a series of ברייתות about the sky. They ask whether the גלגל or the מזלות move, where the sun goes at night, why springs feel warm or cold, and the sun's four seasonal paths. In these, רבי argues with חכמי אומות העולם on one point, and on another he admits their view looks more correct. The גמרא then returns to the משנה and asks why רבי אליעזר does not tell a person at the threshold of the עזרה to step inside, when he gives כרת to an ערל who did not circumcise himself. אביי answers that the דרך רחוקה exemption is only for a fit, pure person. רבא answers that רבי אליעזר's view is reported in different ways: one report measures 'far' from ירושלים, another from the עזרה (our משנה), and the ברייתא about the ערל is a third report, which measures from מודיעים. The amud ends with רבי יוסי הגלילי's ברייתא, which uses a פסוק to show that anywhere from the threshold of the עזרה and outward counts as a 'journey'.

steps.title: The בת קול mocks נבוכדנצר's short lifespan
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues the בת קול's answer to נבוכדנצר. He is a follower of the wicked נמרוד, and a human life is only 70 or 80 years.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The בת קול said to נבוכדנצר: You are a wicked one,] the grandson (disciple) of נמרוד the wicked, who made the whole world rebel against Me during his reign. How many years does a person live? Seventy years, and if he is strong, eighty years, as the פסוק says: 'The days of our years are seventy years, and with strength eighty years.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the ברייתא it brought to challenge רבא. In this part, the בת קול reminds נבוכדנצר how short a human life is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבוכדנצר boasted that he would go up and be like the Most High. The בת קול first shows how little time a person has, only 70 or 80 years. This sets up the next part, where the distances to the heavens are given, to show he could never get there.

keyTerms.meaning: נמרוד the wicked, who led the generation that built מגדל בבל
His grandson; here it means his 'spiritual descendant' or disciple in wickedness
With strength, meaning a person who is unusually healthy

steps.confusionAlert: נבוכדנצר was not literally נמרוד's grandson. The phrase בן בנו means he followed in נמרוד's rebellious ways.

phrases.english: the grandson (disciple) of Nimrod the wicked,
phrases.notes: The בת קול is still answering נבוכדנצר here.

phrases.english: who caused the entire world to rebel
against Me during his reign.
How many are the years of a person?
Seventy years,
and if with strength, eighty years,
as it is stated: 'The days of our years are seventy years'
'and with strength eighty years,'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that began on the previous amud, which the גמרא is using as a challenge to רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement about the thickness of the רקיע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא will give measurements of the heavens that do not match רבא's figure. This step lays the human-lifespan side of the comparison.

steps.title: The huge distances to and between the heavens
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the ground is 500 years' walk from the רקיע. The רקיע is 500 years thick, and each gap between the heavens is another 500 years.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the earth to the first firmament is a walk of five hundred years. The thickness of the firmament is a walk of five hundred years. Between one firmament and the next is a walk of five hundred years, and so too between every firmament. [So how can you climb up there?] 'Rather, you shall be brought down to the grave, to the depths of the pit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the בת קול's answer by listing enormous distances in the heavens. It ends with a פסוק saying נבוכדנצר will go down to the grave, not up to the sky.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who lives 70 or 80 years cannot walk a distance of thousands of years. That is the בת קול's point to נבוכדנצר. For the גמרא's argument, the key detail is that the רקיע is 500 years' walk thick, which is far more than רבא said.

keyTerms.meaning: Firmament; one of the seven heavens
The furthest depths of the pit

steps.whyThisMatters: The phrase 'its thickness is a walk of five hundred years' is exactly what clashes with רבא. This clash is what leads to the תיובתא in the next step.

phrases.english: From the earth to the firmament
is a walk of five hundred years,
and the thickness of the firmament
is a walk of five hundred years,
phrases.notes: This is the detail that contradicts רבא

phrases.english: and between one firmament and the next
is a walk of five hundred years,
and so too between each and every firmament,
'Yet you shall be brought down to the netherworld,'
'to the uttermost parts of the pit.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִן הָאָרֶץ עַד לָרָקִיעַ מַהֲלַךְ חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contrast between the short human lifespan from step 1 and the vast distances of the heavens.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's measurement of the thickness of the רקיע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the רקיע is 500 years' walk thick. That is much larger than the 1,000 פרסאות רבא gave.

steps.title: רבא's view is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא is a תיובתא, a conclusive refutation of רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a conclusive refutation [of רבא].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules that רבא's opinion has been knocked down by the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is offered on behalf of רבא. The ברייתא's figure for the thickness of the רקיע stands, and רבא's smaller figure is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation; the opinion challenged is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: The thickness of the רקיע is 500 years' walk, as the ברייתא says. רבא's view is refuted with a תיובתא.
steps.confusionAlert: תיובתא is a final rejection, not just a question. It means the גמרא found no answer and the opinion falls.

phrases.english: A conclusive refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from the ברייתא quoted in steps 1 and 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's measurement of the רקיע is rejected in favor of the ברייתא.

steps.title: Dispute over whether the sky's sphere or the constellations move
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a dispute. חכמי ישראל say the גלגל is fixed and the מזלות move. חכמי אומות העולם say the גלגל turns and the מזלות are fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: The Jewish Sages say the celestial sphere is fixed and the constellations move around. The sages of the nations of the world say the sphere turns and the constellations are fixed in place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new, related topic about how the sky works. It quotes a ברייתא presenting two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that the stars appear to move across the sky. They disagree about what is actually moving. חכמי ישראל say the stars themselves move within a still sphere. חכמי אומות העולם say the whole sphere turns and carries the stars with it.

keyTerms.meaning: The celestial sphere, the great wheel of the sky

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The Jewish Sages say:
the sphere is fixed, and the constellations revolve.
And the sages of the nations of the world say:
the sphere revolves, and the constellations are fixed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about the structure of the heavens, related by topic to the previous section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute: חכמי ישראל say the גלגל is fixed and the מזלות move, while חכמי אומות העולם say the reverse.

steps.title: רבי's proof from the fixed positions of the constellations
steps.stepSummary: רבי argues against חכמי אומות העולם. The Great Bear is never found in the south, and Scorpio is never found in the north.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: A refutation of their words: We have never found the Great Bear (Ursa Major) in the south, or Scorpio in the north.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי brings a proof to support חכמי ישראל and reject the view of חכמי אומות העולם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the whole sphere turned, רבי reasons, the stars on it would sometimes swing around to the opposite side of the sky. Since the Great Bear always stays in the north and Scorpio always stays in the south, the stars must be moving in place rather than being carried around by a turning sphere.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'Wagon': the constellation Ursa Major (the Great Bear), seen in the north
Scorpio, a constellation seen in the south

phrases.english: Rabbi said: A refutation of their words:
we have never found
Ursa Major in the south
or Scorpio in the north.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the view of חכמי ישראל from step 4 against חכמי אומות העולם.
steps.raayaObject: That the גלגל is fixed and the מזלות move, as חכמי ישראל say
steps.raayaSupportSource: Observation: the Great Bear always stays in the north and Scorpio always stays in the south

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב shows the proof does not hold
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב suggests the constellations could stay in place even if things around them turn. They could be like the center socket of a millstone or the pivot of a door.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב objects to this: But perhaps it is like the socket of a millstone [which stays in place while the stone turns around it]. Or perhaps it is like the pivot of a door [which stays in place while the door swings around it].
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב challenges רבי's proof. He shows that the observation can be explained even according to חכמי אומות העולם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A millstone turns, but its center socket stays in one spot. A door swings, but its pivot stays put. In the same way, the turning sphere could have fixed points, so the Great Bear and Scorpio could always stay in their places even while the sphere turns. That means רבי's observation does not prove his point.

keyTerms.meaning: The central socket of a millstone, which stays still while the stone turns
The pivot of a door, which stays still while the door swings

steps.whatToRemember: רבי tried to prove חכמי ישראל's view from the fixed positions of the constellations. רב אחא בר יעקב showed the proof can be pushed off, because a turning sphere can still have points that stay in place.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אחא בר יעקב does not say חכמי ישראל are wrong. He only says רבי's specific proof does not settle the question.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov strongly objects to it:
But perhaps it is like the socket of a millstone.
phrases.notes: The center stays put while the stone turns around it

phrases.english: Alternatively, like the pivot of a door.
phrases.notes: The pivot stays put while the door swings

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: וְדִילְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof רבי brought in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רבי's proof is rejected, not the view of חכמי ישראל itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A turning sphere can still have fixed points, so the constant positions of the constellations do not prove the sphere is still.

steps.title: Where the sun goes at night
steps.stepSummary: Both groups agree the sun travels beneath the רקיע by day. They disagree about night: חכמי ישראל say it goes above the רקיע, while חכמי אומות העולם say it goes beneath the earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Jewish sages say: By day the sun travels below the רקיע, and at night above the רקיע. The sages of the nations say: By day the sun travels below the רקיע, and at night below the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second astronomy dispute between חכמי ישראל and חכמי אומות העולם, this time about the sun's path at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree about daytime, so the only question is where the sun is when we can't see it. One view says it is hidden above the sky-dome. The other says it circles underneath the earth to the other side.

phrases.english: The Jewish sages say:

phrases.aramaic: בַּיּוֹם חַמָּה מְהַלֶּכֶת לְמַטָּה מִן הָרָקִיעַ,
phrases.english: By day the sun travels beneath the firmament,
and at night above the firmament.
And the sages of the nations of the world say:

phrases.aramaic: בַּיּוֹם חַמָּה מְהַלֶּכֶת לְמַטָּה מִן הָרָקִיעַ,
phrases.english: By day the sun travels beneath the firmament,
and at night beneath the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel dispute to the one in step 4, using the same two groups of sages
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is only about the night: the sun is either above the רקיע or beneath the earth.

steps.title: רבי sides with the non-Jewish sages because of the springs
steps.stepSummary: רבי says the view of חכמי אומות העולם seems more correct. Springs are cold by day and warm at night, which suggests the sun warms them from underneath at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: Their words seem more correct than ours, because by day springs are cold and at night they are hot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי brings evidence from nature to decide the dispute, and he decides in favor of the non-Jewish sages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spring water comes from deep inside the earth. If it feels warm at night, the sun must be passing beneath the ground and heating it. That fits חכמי אומות העולם better than the idea that the sun goes above the רקיע.

keyTerms.meaning: Their words appear more correct than ours

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי openly accepts the view of non-Jewish scholars when the evidence supports it. Notice the contrast with step 5, where he argued against them.

phrases.english: Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi) said:
And their words appear more correct than ours,
since by day springs are cold,
and at night they are hot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings evidence to decide the dispute in step 7
steps.raayaObject: The view of חכמי אומות העולם that the sun travels beneath the earth at night
steps.raayaSupportSource: Observation that springs are cold by day and warm at night

steps.title: רבי נתן explains summer and winter temperatures
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן teaches that in summer the sun is high, so the world is hot and springs are cold. In winter the sun is low, so the world is cold and springs are warm.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: In summer the sun travels high in the sky, so the whole world is hot and springs are cold. In winter the sun travels at the low edges of the sky, so the whole world is cold and springs are hot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related ברייתא that uses the same idea of warm and cold springs, this time to explain the seasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 explained day versus night. Here רבי נתן explains summer versus winter with the same pattern: the air and the springs are always opposite. When the sun is high, the surface heats up. When it is low, the depths stay warmer than the air.

keyTerms.meaning: The low edges of the sky

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Natan says:
In the summer,
the sun travels high in the sky,
therefore the entire world is hot
and springs are cold.
In the winter,
the sun travels at the low edges of the sky,
therefore the entire world is cold
and springs are hot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the spring-temperature idea from day and night to the seasons
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sun's height in each season explains why the air and the springs feel opposite in temperature.

steps.title: The sun's four seasonal paths
steps.stepSummary: The sun follows four paths, one for each group of three months. Each path serves a purpose: melting snow, ripening fruit, drying rivers, and sparing newly planted seeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: The sun travels in four paths. In ניסן, אייר, and סיון it travels over the mountains to melt the snows. In תמוז, אב, and אלול it travels over inhabited land to ripen the fruit. In תשרי, מרחשון, and כסלו it travels over the seas to dry up the rivers. In טבת, שבט, and אדר it travels over the desert so as not to dry out the seeds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one last astronomy ברייתא, describing where the sun travels in each season and why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a purpose to the sun's movement. Each season's path benefits the world. In the last season, the point is that the sun stays away from the fields so it does not harm the young seeds.
steps.whatToRemember: The astronomy section closes here. Its main points: the sun travels beneath the earth at night (רבי's view), its height explains the seasons (רבי נתן), and it has four seasonal paths (רבנן).

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The sun travels in four paths.
Nisan, Iyyar, and Sivan:

phrases.aramaic: מְהַלֶּכֶת בֶּהָרִים, כְּדֵי לְפַשֵּׁר אֶת הַשְּׁלָגִין.
phrases.english: it travels over the mountains, in order to melt the snows.
Tammuz, Av, and Elul:

phrases.aramaic: מְהַלֶּכֶת בַּיִּשּׁוּב, כְּדֵי לְבַשֵּׁל אֶת הַפֵּירוֹת.
phrases.english: it travels over the settled land, in order to ripen the fruit.
Tishrei, Marcheshvan, and Kislev:

phrases.aramaic: מְהַלֶּכֶת בַּיַּמִּים, כְּדֵי לְיַבֵּשׁ אֶת הַנְּהָרוֹת.
phrases.english: it travels over the seas, in order to dry up the rivers.
Tevet, Shevat, and Adar:

phrases.aramaic: מְהַלֶּכֶת בַּמִּדְבָּר, שֶׁלֹּא לְיַבֵּשׁ אֶת הַזְּרָעִים.
phrases.english: it travels over the desert, so as not to dry out the seeds.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּאַרְבָּעָה שְׁבִילִין חַמָּה מְהַלֶּכֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the seasonal theme with a full map of the sun's yearly paths
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sun follows four seasonal paths, and each one benefits the world.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי אליעזר's threshold rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves astronomy and quotes the משנה again. There, רבי אליעזר says anyone from the threshold of the עזרה and outward counts as being on a דרך רחוקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר says: From the threshold (of the עזרה and outward), etc.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא returns to the משנה by quoting רבי אליעזר's opinion so it can question it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, someone on a דרך רחוקה at the time of the קרבן פסח brings פסח שני instead. רבי אליעזר sets the line very close: anyone even just outside the threshold of the עזרה counts as 'far away.'

keyTerms.meaning: Etc., meaning the rest of the quote from the משנה
A distant journey, which exempts one from the first פסח

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for a link to the astronomy section. The גמרא is simply going back to the משנה after a long side discussion.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer says
from the threshold, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the astronomy side discussion and returns to the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, anyone outside the threshold of the עזרה is on a דרך רחוקה.

steps.title: Why not tell him to walk in? Contradiction from the uncircumcised Jew
steps.stepSummary: If the person could easily step into the עזרה, why don't we tell him to go in? After all, רבי אליעזר himself says an uncircumcised Jew who does not circumcise himself gets כרת, which means he expects a person to act so he can bring the קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though he is able to enter, we don't say to him, 'Get up and enter'?! But it was taught: A Jew who is uncircumcised and did not circumcise himself is punished with כרת. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר's ruling in the משנה using another ruling of his own from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר lets the person stay passive just outside the threshold. In the ברייתא, he punishes an ערל with כרת for not fixing his situation, which means he expects a person to take action to become fit for the פסח. The two rulings seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: That he is able to enter

steps.confusionAlert: The כרת here is not for being uncircumcised in general. It is for missing the קרבן פסח, since an ערל may not eat it and he could have fixed that.

phrases.english: And even though he is able to enter,
we don't say to him: Get up and enter?!
But wasn't it taught:
An uncircumcised Jew who did not circumcise himself
is punished with karet,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּמָצֵי עָיֵיל, וְלָא אָמְרִינַן לֵיהּ קוּם עֱיֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of רבי אליעזר quoted in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling that a person just outside the threshold counts as on a דרך רחוקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר's other ruling (כרת for an ערל who doesn't circumcise) shows he requires a person to act so he becomes fit for the פסח. So he should also require this person to step into the עזרה.

steps.title: אביי: The distant-journey exemption is for a pure person
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the דרך רחוקה exemption applies to a pure person, not to an impure or unfit person.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: the 'distant journey' exemption is for a pure person. There is no 'distant journey' exemption for an impure person.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge from Step 12. He explains how רבי אליעזר can say a person at the threshold is exempt and also say an uncircumcised person gets כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases are different. A pure, fit person who stands outside the עזרה is exempt because of where he is, and nobody forces him to walk in. An uncircumcised or otherwise unfit person has a personal problem that he must fix, so he does not get the distance exemption, and that is why he can get כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: a 'distant journey', which exempts a person from the first פסח
ritually pure, fit to bring the קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume אביי is talking only about טומאה. He uses 'impure' to mean anyone who has a personal problem that blocks him from the קרבן, and that includes the ערל from Step 12.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The 'distant journey' exemption is for a pure person,
and there is no 'distant journey' exemption for an impure person.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between two cases (pure versus unfit)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי אליעזר expects the ערל to act, he should also expect the person at the threshold to step in.
steps.terutzMaskana: The distance exemption belongs only to a fit, pure person. An unfit person has to fix himself and is not covered by it.

steps.title: רבא: Two traditions of רבי אליעזר, the first measuring from Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the two statements come from two different traditions of רבי אליעזר. The first tradition measures 'distant' as outside the place where the פסח is eaten, like מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: this is a dispute between תנאים. A ברייתא teaches that רבי אליעזר says: 'distance of place' is written about the פסח, and 'distance of place' is written about מעשר. There it means outside the place where it is eaten, so here too it means outside the place where it is eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to Step 12. He says there are two versions of what רבי אליעזר held, and he quotes the first version here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני may be eaten anywhere in ירושלים, so in this report 'far' means outside ירושלים. Applying the same rule to פסח, anyone inside ירושלים is not 'far' and is obligated. The ברייתא about the ערל is a separate, third report of רבי אליעזר: as רש״י and תוספות explain, it holds that only someone outside מודיעים counts as 'far.' Our משנה's threshold rule comes from yet another report, measured from the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: here, מעשר שני, which is eaten only in ירושלים
outside the place where it is eaten

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא move: instead of reconciling two statements of one תנא, the גמרא says students reported his view in two different ways.

phrases.english: Rava said: it is a dispute between Tannaim.
As it was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Eliezer says:
'Distance of place' is stated regarding the Pesach,
and 'distance of place' is stated regarding the tithe.
Just as there it means outside the place where it is eaten,
so too here it means outside the place where it is eaten.
phrases.notes: The פסח is eaten in all of ירושלים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from אביי's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two different traditions of the same תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements must come from one consistent view of רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר's view is reported in different ways: 'far' means outside ירושלים, outside the עזרה (our משנה), or, in the ברייתא about the ערל, outside מודיעים. So the משנה and the כרת statement need not match.

steps.title: The second tradition: measured from the place where the offering is done
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה reports that רבי אליעזר measured 'far' as outside the place where the פסח is offered, meaning the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי אליעזר: it means outside the place where it is performed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the second version of רבי אליעזר's view. It finishes רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'far' is measured from the עזרה, where the פסח is slaughtered, not from ירושלים. This version matches our משנה, which says anyone from the threshold of the עזרה and outward is 'far'.

keyTerms.meaning: outside the place where it is performed (the עזרה)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three reports of רבי אליעזר's view. In one, 'far' means outside ירושלים, where the פסח is eaten. In another, from רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה, 'far' means outside the עזרה, where it is offered, and that is our משנה. The ברייתא about the ערל is a third report, where 'far' means outside מודיעים.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Yehuda says
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:
outside the place of its performance.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the ברייתא that רבא quoted
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The distant-journey exemption applies to anyone outside the עזרה.

steps.title: Whose view is the rule about counting the impure majority in the courtyard?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which view supports רבי יצחק בר רב יוסף's rule: to decide whether the majority is impure, count only the people standing in the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this follow? רבי יצחק בר רב יוסף said: regarding impure people, follow the majority of those standing in the עזרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related rule and asks which tradition of רבי אליעזר it fits. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If most of the people are impure, the פסח may be brought in טומאה. רבי יצחק בר רב יוסף counts only the people in the עזרה and ignores people elsewhere in ירושלים. So the עזרה must be the place that defines who counts.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is this

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר רַב יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yitzchak bar Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: בִּטְמֵאִים הַלֵּךְ אַחַר רוֹב הָעוֹמְדִין בָּעֲזָרָה.
phrases.english: Regarding impure people, follow the majority of those standing in the courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the two traditions to find the source of a later rule
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which tradition of רבי אליעזר supports counting only those in the עזרה

steps.title: It follows רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה's tradition
steps.stepSummary: The rule follows רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה's version of רבי אליעזר, which makes the עזרה the defining place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view? It follows רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה, who spoke in the name of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The counting rule fits the tradition that measures from the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that tradition, what matters for the פסח is whether a person is in the עזרה. So only the people standing there count toward the impure majority. In the other tradition, everyone in ירושלים would be part of the group and would count.
steps.whatToRemember: The עזרה tradition of רבי אליעזר, reported by רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה, explains both our משנה's threshold rule and רבי יצחק בר רב יוסף's rule to count only those in the עזרה.

phrases.aramaic: כְּמַאן — כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: In accordance with whom? In accordance with Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Yehuda,
who spoke in the name of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן — כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule follows רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה's tradition that the עזרה is the defining place.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יוסי's line in the משנה about the dot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening words of רבי יוסי's statement in the משנה: 'Therefore, etc.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יוסי said to him, 'Therefore', and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the next piece of the משנה so it can discuss it. This is a setup line that prepares the ברייתא coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יוסי explains that there is a dot over the ה of רחוקה. The dot tells us 'distant' does not mean really far, only outside the threshold of the עזרה. The word 'וכו׳' tells us to fill in the rest of the משנה from memory.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore. This opens רבי יוסי's explanation of the dot.
Etc. The rest of the quote is shortened.
Dotted. Refers to the dot over the ה in רְחוֹקָה, which is the subject of this line of the משנה.

steps.confusionAlert: The רבי יוסי in the משנה (רבי יוסי, son of חלפתא) is not the same person as רבי יוסי הגלילי in the ברייתא that comes next. They have similar names but are different תנאים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said to him:
Therefore, etc.
phrases.notes: The quote is cut short: the dot over the ה shows 'distant' isn't really far, just from the threshold of the עזרה and outward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of רבי אליעזר's two traditions and the counting rule to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dot over the ה of רחוקה shows that 'distant' means only outside the threshold of the עזרה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי proves from a פסוק that a 'journey' starts at the עזרה's threshold
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: you might think 'דרך' means a two- or three-day trip. But the פסוק 'ובדרך לא היה' uses plain 'דרך,' which teaches that anywhere from the threshold of the עזרה and outward is called a journey.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי הגלילי says, from the word 'journey' I would have understood a walk of two or three days. But when the פסוק says 'and was not on a journey' (without the word 'distant'), it teaches that from the threshold of the עזרה and outward is called a journey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives a פסוק as the source for the משנה's view. 'Journey' here does not mean far away. It means simply being outside the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First comes the הוה אמינא: the word 'דרך' sounds like real travel of several days. But במדבר ט:יג describes the person who must bring the פסח as one who 'was not on a journey,' and it leaves out the word 'distant.' So the exemption applies to anyone who is not in the עזרה, starting from its threshold.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have understood. Introduces the first, mistaken reading.
It teaches. Introduces what the פסוק actually shows.
The threshold of the Temple courtyard.

steps.whatToRemember: The 'דרך רחוקה' exemption from קרבן פסח does not require real distance. Being anywhere from the threshold of the עזרה and outward at the time of שחיטה counts as 'on a journey.' This is the view of רבי אליעזר, supported by רבי יוסי's dot and רבי יוסי הגלילי's פסוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: This makes the עזרה the defining place for 'journey.' That fits the approach from Step 17, where the עזרה is what counts.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
From 'journey,' I would understand
a walk of two or three days.
When it says 'and was not on a journey,'
it teaches that from the threshold of the courtyard
phrases.notes: The starting line is the edge of the עזרה.

phrases.english: and outward is called a journey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוסי's statement in the משנה with a scriptural derivation from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The view that 'דרך רחוקה' means anywhere from the threshold of the עזרה and outward.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי יוסי הגלילי, reading 'ובדרך לא היה' (במדבר ט:יג), which leaves out the word 'distant.'
